problem: Decision-time planning with action-conditioned world models (MPC+CEM) scores candidates only by how close the predicted terminal state is to the goal, so it cannot detect predicted trajectories whose intermediate transitions are not realizable in the real environment; predicted goal-reaching then fails in actual rollout.
motivation: Improving the world model side (bigger video backbones, action guidance) is costly or requires probabilistic formulations that do not fit deterministic JEPA latent predictors, and none of it fixes the terminal-only cost. In embodied control, consecutive observations tightly constrain the action between them, so an inverse dynamics model can check per-step realizability without touching the world model.
key_idea: Use an inverse dynamics model as a decision-time verifier: penalize the per-step mismatch between the conditioning action and the action inferred from the predicted transition (cycle action consistency), added to the goal cost with a scale-invariant adaptive weight.
insight: The consistency term filters candidates that reach a goal-like predicted state via unrealizable transitions, giving gains on all world models and tasks (largest on deformable Rope: chamfer 1.38 to 0.56). The adaptive weight w_a = lambda*sigma_g/sigma_a matters because cost spreads vary across world models, tasks and CEM iterations: no single constant weight improved all three tasks on Le-WM, while the adaptive one gave the best total (+20). Gains also make search cheaper: with N=30 samples, ACID matches or exceeds the N=300 baseline on Reacher.
method: Cycle action consistency cost: c_a = (1/H) sum_t ||a_t - G_phi(z_hat_t, z_hat_{t+1})||^2, reusing the same predicted latent trajectory (no extra world-model rollout).
IDM verifier G_phi: flow-matching action decoder (pi0-style prefix-suffix transformer, 4 layers, 3 heads, width 192) taking two consecutive latents; one Euler step at inference (ten for NWM).
Augmented cost: c = c_g + w_a*c_a, replacing the goal cost in CEM/MPC; world model and planner unchanged.

Scale-invariant adaptive weight: w_a = lambda*sigma_g/sigma_a recomputed each CEM iteration from std of costs across the N candidates; lambda tuned once per world model (0.07 Le-WM/PLDM, 0.5 DINO-WM, 0.08 NWM).
IDM training: separate IDM per task on the world model's offline dataset with frozen encoder latents, 200K steps, batch 256, AdamW lr 1e-4, actions standardized.

setting.backbone: Frozen action-conditioned world models (Le-WM, PLDM, DINO-WM, NWM w/ CompACT) planned with CEM + separately trained flow-matching IDM verifier
setting.training_data: IDM trained on each task's offline trajectories (e.g., 20k PushT episodes, 10k Reacher, 10k OGBench-Cube, 1k Rope, 1k Granular, RECON navigation); world models used as released/trained with original recipes
setting.observation: monocular RGB images (current and goal image), encoded to latents
setting.action_space: continuous low-level actions per task (planned H-step sequences via CEM); navigation uses continuous waypoint-style actions
setting.simulator: PushT, DeepMind Control Reacher, OGBench Cube, Nvidia Flex (Rope/Granular); RECON offline real-world dataset for navigation
setting.privileged: none (goal image given as in standard goal-conditioned setting)

numbers.extra: baseline ATE 1.3141, RPE 0.3831; 1 CEM step, 80 samples
numbers.evidence: Table 2 right: NWM w/ CompACT Ours 1.2835 (-2.3%), 0.3773 (-1.5%)

numbers_note: Only the fixed-benchmark tables of world-model planning tasks; not standard VLN/ObjNav benchmarks. Splits are 'test' as a placeholder since none named.
results: ACID improves every world model on all six tasks: success rate gains of +4 to +14 points with Le-WM/PLDM (e.g. Reacher PLDM 76 to 90), chamfer distance cut 1.38 to 0.56 on Rope with DINO-WM, and small navigation gains on NWM (ATE -2.3%). With 30 CEM samples it matches the 300-sample baseline on Reacher.
limitations: Relies on consecutive observations identifying the action; weakens under partial observability or exogenous perturbations.
Requires a separately trained per-task IDM; overhead per step up to ~39% of world-model latency (DINO-WM).
Modest gain on navigation, small evaluation sets (10 instances for Rope/Granular, 50 episodes-scale for others).
